title: jQuery and the Browser-Compatibility Crisis (2006)
explainer: In January 2006, John Resig released jQuery specifically to paper over the inconsistent DOM and JavaScript behavior across the browsers of the day, building on earlier work like Dean Edwards' cssQuery library. It's a clean case study in why developer tools and frameworks actually get built: not to add new capability, but to give developers one stable interface over a fragmented platform underneath.

title: Ruby on Rails: A Framework Extracted From a Real App (2004)
explainer: David Heinemeier Hansson didn't design Rails on a blank page; he extracted it from patterns he had already built solving real problems in Basecamp at the company 37signals, open-sourcing the result in July 2004. That path, pulling a reusable framework out of a working application rather than designing one up front, is a recurring and instructive way durable developer tools actually come into being.
